cards.note: External plugin already delivered as a plain npm package: main/exports plus dsh.bundle.patch, installed through the official profile path; no repository-plugins config or legacy manifest in the tree.
Manifest declares dsh.client ({platform: web, inject}) only; no legacy dshClient field and no dsh.plugin.json anywhere in the tree.
dsh.client with platform web plus exports["./client"] make the bundle scannable; the alpha.2 boot manifest composes the row (runtime-verified).

Every consumed service is declared: host inject ['tools'] (the elided real body additionally documents webServer + connection), client inject ['slots','locale']; nothing is reached through an undeclared ctx.get or property read.
The optional better-locale service stays a weak ctx.get probe with graceful degradation, never a hard inject entry.
The plugin subscribes to no session/event stream and derives no session state from event fields.
The browser half is not a self-rendering session client; it reads the plugin's own /api/mcp-manager routes, not ctx.sessions.
No task/run output tailing; the panel's tool browse uses ctx.tools.schemas(), which is unaffected.
Host half already names the post-0812 service webServer (and connection); no httpServer/tasks/onTaskDone identifiers remain anywhere.
The plugin uses no ImageAttachmentRef, read_image output, or image metadata schema.
read_image is neither registered, wrapped, parsed, nor snapshot-tested here.
No custom DeepSeek LLM adapter, image interceptor, or attachment/upload cache in the plugin.

The browser panel talks to the plugin's own webServer routes; the documented surface never uses the removed Host APIProxy (card's own warning against importing host-internal client packages honoured).
Target is alpha.2 (which restores the semantics) and the plugin produces no persisted SessionEvents.
No host source patch and no import from internal session-view paths; the plugin stays on public services.
Host-plane contract now resolves the profile layer from the runtime (ctx.baseUrl anchored at the active profile directory, optional dshHomePath service) instead of a hardcoded profiles/web path.
No headless wrapper, process supervisor, or stdout/stderr parser in this repository.
No tool presentation mode, PTC preset, or dispatch-waterfall usage.
Not a permission/approval/WebFetch policy or audit plugin.

The custom /api/mcp-manager routes are documented to call ctx.connection.requestRejection(req) first (connection added to the real body's inject list); route bodies are elided in this fixture, so the contract is carried in the host-plane comment.
Not a model provider plugin; no login-configuration seat involved.

Optional capability. The plugin already registers its namespace through the public ctx.locale.register and keeps extra languages as an optional third-party better-locale probe, not a custom i18n patch to retire.
No subagent orchestration or selector surface.
Deployment/adapter-level privacy behaviour; the plugin neither ships nor configures the official DeepSeek adapter.
No persistent PowerShell/Bash or Windows directory-picker compatibility workarounds are carried.
Session-log upload is a deployment decision for whoever installs the bundle; the plugin configures no telemetry rows.
The repository ships no browser acceptance script or wrapper; its release procedure is manual. (The recipe was used for this migration's own verification, not added to the tree.)
No structured-question answerer is registered.
No agent-preset inference from persisted sessions; the plugin sets no agent-preset roots.
isTokenDelta / TPS computation is not used.
The bundle patch inserts only its own row; it does not restate or maintain the dsh-base composition, so it carries no telemetry stance to override.
@earendil-works/pi-ai is not imported or depended on.

@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-runtime removed from both peerDependencies and dsh.client.inject; the client Context is @deepseek-ai/cordis and the ctx.slots/ctx.locale owners (ui-renderer, locale) are declared as peers.

All three ids agree on the bare package name: __ModuleLoader__.load registration id, the insert row name, and package.json#name; the real alpha.2 boot manifest carries "id":"@bench/dsh-bench-mcpanel" and the combo artifact registers the same id.
The panel reads no session timeline or user-message content.
No composer DOM manipulation.
The panel renders no MarkdownText or fenced CodeBlocks (its documented primitives are Button/Input/Pill).
ctx.connection.api is not consumed; panel data comes from the plugin's own host routes.
No subagent descriptor construction or subagent/descriptor assertions.
ctx.workspaces navigation methods (connectWorkspace/startSession/pickDirectory/listDirectory/createDirectory) are not used.
The plugin produces no third-party persisted SessionEvents.
No ctx.remote calls or Remote failure handling; the browser half uses its own webServer routes.

Peer cohort re-pinned to ^0.1.2-alpha.2 and matched to the packages actually consumed (client-plane owners added, removed dsh-client-runtime); every @deepseek-ai/dsh-* peer is flagged optional so npm never auto-installs a later prerelease of the same line (0.1.2-rc.1) beside the target — the host/profile provides those packages, and the ranges still sit on the cohort floor for the dependency contract. Install at the release cutoff (plain npm install, then the pinned --before install) now resolves clean with no ETARGET.
No startup wrapper or CI matrix carries Node 22 forcing / dsh-web skipping workarounds; verification ran on Node 24.21.0.
pluginInventory/list snapshots are not consumed or validated.
The client half reads no Host home/loopback facts (no host.describe, no $host usage).
The bundle patch mounts no dsh-tool-todo/subagent/agent/terminal-bash rows and lists none of them as peers; the shipped profile supplies session-projection.
The host half registers no settings namespace; its registry lives in the profile patch layer, not in ctx.settings.
